questions.q: In the United States, which is the most common unit for comparing energy sources or fuels?
options: Kilowatthour
British thermal unit (Btu)
Barrel
Short ton
questions.explain: Converting fuels to a common unit lets you compare them directly.
questions.evidence: In the United States, Btu is the most common unit for comparing energy sources or fuels.

questions.q: Which of these is energy conservation rather than energy efficiency?
options: Installing energy-efficient lights
Buying a more efficient boiler
Insulating a building
Turning lights off when they are not needed
questions.explain: Efficiency does the same job with less energy; conservation avoids using energy at all.
questions.evidence: installing energy-efficient lights is an efficiency measure, and turning lights off when not needed, either manually or with timers or motion sensor switches, is conservation.

questions.q: Why is electricity called a secondary energy source?
options: It is produced by converting primary sources such as coal, gas, nuclear, solar and wind
It is less important than oil
It is always produced second, after heat
It can only be stored in batteries
questions.explain: The losses of that conversion are part of why saving electricity matters.
questions.evidence: The electricity we use is a secondary energy source because it is produced by converting primary sources of energy such as coal, natural gas, nuclear energy, solar energy, and wind energy into electrical power.

questions.q: Which home energy uses continue all year round?
options: Space heating and air conditioning
Swimming-pool heating only
Water heating, lighting and refrigeration
Garden lighting only
questions.explain: Heating and cooling are seasonal; these uses are constant.
questions.evidence: Water heating, lighting, and refrigeration are year-round home energy uses.

questions.q: What is manufacturing, as an energy-using industrial activity?
options: Extracting coal, oil and gas
The physical, mechanical or chemical transformation of materials into new products
Growing crops
Building roads and houses
questions.explain: Industry also includes agriculture, mining and construction.
questions.evidence: Manufacturing is the physical, mechanical, or chemical transformation of materials or substances into new products.

questions.q: What is the UK Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (ESOS)?
options: A grant for home insulation
A voluntary green label for products
A tax on electricity bills
A mandatory energy assessment scheme for UK organisations that meet the qualification criteria
questions.explain: Qualifying organisations must assess their energy use and report opportunities.
questions.evidence: is a mandatory energy assessment scheme for organisations in the UK that meet the qualification criteria.

questions.q: What is an ESOS assessment designed to identify?
options: Tailored, cost-effective measures to save energy and achieve carbon and cost savings
Which staff use the most electricity
The cheapest energy supplier
Buildings to sell
questions.explain: The audit points to savings that make business sense.
questions.evidence: The ESOS assessment is designed to identify tailored and cost-effective measures that allow participating businesses to save energy and achieve carbon and cost savings.

questions.q: What is 'de minimis' energy consumption under ESOS?
options: Energy used outside working hours
Energy from renewable sources
The maximum 5% of total energy consumption that may be excluded from audits
The smallest site in the organisation
questions.explain: At least 95% of energy use must be covered by audits or another compliance route.
questions.evidence: The maximum 5% of total energy consumption that may be excluded from any audit or alternative compliance measures is known as your ‘de minimis’ energy consumption.

questions.q: How must an energy intensity ratio be expressed?
options: As a percentage of the energy bill
In kWh per unit of an activity indicator, for example kWh/m² of floor area
In pounds per employee
As the number of energy audits per year
questions.explain: Ratios let you compare energy use as an organisation grows or shrinks.
questions.evidence: The units for any energy intensity ratio must be expressed in kWh /x

questions.q: If verifiable data for an indicator is not available, what should you do?
options: Leave the indicator out of the audit
Copy last year's figure without explanation
Ask the regulator for an exemption
Use a reasonable estimate and record the estimation method in your evidence pack
questions.explain: Methods include direct comparison, pro-rata extrapolation and benchmarking.
questions.evidence: If verifiable data is not available, you should use a reasonable estimate and keep a record of the method used to estimate the indicator in your evidence pack.

questions.q: If energy data is not in your accounting system, what does the guidance suggest?
options: Nominate a person to record energy use and costs
Stop monitoring energy until the system is upgraded
Estimate everything at year end
Rely on the supplier's marketing data
questions.explain: Reliable monitoring is the foundation of any energy audit.
questions.evidence: If the data is not included in your accounting system, nominate a person to record energy use and costs.

questions.q: What should investment, equipment replacement and maintenance decisions consider?
options: Only the purchase price
Only the energy saved in the first month
The full cost to the organisation
Whatever the supplier recommends
questions.explain: Life-cycle cost analysis compares options over their whole working life.
questions.evidence: It is helpful to ensure that investment decisions and equipment replacement or maintenance decisions consider the full cost to the organisation.
